transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Mrs. Al-Rashid, I wanted to stop in and talk to you about your chemotherapy session from this morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh, hello doctor. Is everything okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have some things I need to discuss with you. First, I want to say that I am sorry. Our team made a mistake with your dose today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? I do not understand. Was the medicine wrong?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion with how the dose was calculated. The amount you received wasn't exactly what we intended for your current weight.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I... I don't understand. I thought you were the experts. Did I receive too much?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Things didn't go quite right with the calculation process. I apologize for this. Now, the most important thing is that we are monitoring you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel very dizzy. This is very frightening. I trusted that you knew—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right, let's look at your vitals quickly. We need to make sure your blood pressure is stable.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But you have not told me what happened. Why was there a mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a systemic issue with how the weight was recorded in the chart. I am sorry that this happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I have lost so much weight because of the sickness. Did you not see that I am thinner?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But looking at the monitor, your heart rate is fine.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel a great deal of shame that this has happened to me. I just wanted to get well.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Now, as for the next steps, we are going to keep you on a continuous IV drip of fluids for the next twenty-four hours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will this make me more sick?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The fluids will help your kidneys clear the extra medicine from your system. You just need to stay in the bed and let the nurses check your urine output every two hours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do I need more medicine to fix this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, just the fluids. I'll have the nurse come in and start that now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot believe this. I feel so shaken. My family will be so worried when they—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Look, I actually have to go check on another patient who is crashing in room four, so we have to wrap this up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are leaving? But I am still so confused.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The plan is the fluids. The nurse will be here in ten minutes.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not know what to think.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've told you I'm sorry. Just follow the nurse's instructions with the IV.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is it dangerous?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are monitoring you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel very small in this hospital.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I really have to run now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, doctor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will check on you again this evening.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Good. Just stay in bed.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('wrap this up', 'have to run now') and interrupts the patient's emotional distress to check vitals.

E.justification: Resident uses platitudes ('things didn't go quite right', 'some confusion') and never explicitly names the error (e.g., 'overdose') despite patient asking.

A.justification: While the resident says 'I am sorry', responsibility is deflected to a 'systemic issue with how the weight was recorded in the chart'.

R.justification: Resident uses generic validation ('I understand') but fails to name specific emotions or engage with the patient's emotional bids.

T.justification: Resident provides a specific next step (IV fluids), a timeline (next twenty-four hours), and a patient role (stay in bed/let nurses check urine).
